plaintext.source: No decipherment bound with it; not in CSP Spain vol. 2.

transcription.notes: Only the second cipher paragraph of f. 141r transcribed.

plaintext.source: Contemporary decipherments of CSP 534, 540/541 and 544 in the same volume (ff. 190, 342-343, 424-430), calendared in English by Bergenroth, CSP Spain vol. 2; not imaged in these DECODE records.

system.summary: The Sessa-Charles V nomenclator of 1523-25: three-letter code groups for words and syllables plus a letter alphabet with homophones, a clear/cipher switch sign and a null paragraph opener.
system.sibling_key: Identical to the sessa1524 cipher; its key (targets/sessa1524/key_working.md) applies unchanged.
system.notes: Recognised at sight from the recurring groups gap, sof, suf, qib, mus, kef, dim, cob, coh, bas, Jap.

prior_solution.where: Contemporary decipherments of four of the letters in RAH Salazar A-27, calendared in Bergenroth, CSP Spain vol. 2 nos. 534, 540, 541, 544 (1866); R9660 and R9665 not calendared

conditions.human_role: Set the goal; the DECODE cookie saved earlier fetched the images

solution.what: Fetched metadata and all 55 openings of R9660-R9666 with the saved DECODE cookie; read every date line.
Recognised the cipher as the sessa1524 nomenclator from recurring code groups.
Matched the letters to Bergenroth CSP Spain vol. 2 nos. 534, 540, 541, 544, 545 (Salazar A-27 folios); R9660 and R9665 not calendared.
Read the second cipher paragraph of R9660 f. 141r with the 1524 key; about half the tokens resolve.

R9665 ff. 437-438: three cipher runs read with the sessa1524 key; the f. 437r margin note (Su Sd. por esta bula es declarado contra Francia) matches token for token and gives hef = por; two f. 437v runs carry interlinear decipherments of the time.
R9660 ff. 141r-147r (7 openings, ~2,050 cipher tokens) transcribed line by line from full-size strips by two subagents, each reading with the sessa1524 key.
Checked the R9660 margin notes as cribs: they are copyist insertions of omitted text, not decipherments.
Key extended from R9660 context: yim duque, bla ir, boz -io, loz obisp-, z o, q l, 9 e/l, gam como (probable), ruc a verb root; values cross-applied between the two halves.
R9660 read in part: ~57% of tokens resolve; ~150 code groups open with no decipherment on DECODE to value them.

Statistical validation (docs/_validate.py): 2004 tokens, 139 types, es-golden-age order 4: reading -2.273 per letter; random keys -3.661 (z 6.5); key annealed onto shuffled ciphertext best -2.319 (mean -2.341, z 5.0); annealer on the real text -2.215. Verdict: pass.

Full texts listed in outcome.texts (George Lasry's request of 22 Oct 2026): reading_r9660.txt and reading_r9665.txt (cipher line with reading); key = sessa1524/key_working.md (linked); R9661-R9664 not transcribed (calendared in CSP Spain 2)

Reading audit (George Lasry's sentence test): reading_r9660.txt read through; nearly every line carries open groups or spelled letters, only phrases can be built (10% of sentences clean, docs/_check_reading.py). R9660 relabelled decoded, not read; R9665's three glossed runs kept as read (reviewed B). fraction_read 0.55 -> ~0.02 (estimated).

Re-read b34: looked for a text of R9660. DECODE: the seven RAH 9/27 records (R9660-R9666, harvest batch_3.json) and the neighbouring records R9656-R9659, R9667-R9669 fetched; none holds a decipherment. f. 141r is marked 'Dup.da' (the duplicate). CSP Spain 2 (archive.org OCR) grepped for February 1523: no Sessa letter of 20 Feb.

Applied the sessa1524 key values of passes 16, 17 and b23 to R9660's decode (research/reading_audit/b34_sessa_apply.py -> reading_r9660_b34.txt): 64 occurrences of 32 groups; net, len, boz, var, pof, Jam, nah, leg, bun, lin, hut read in every R9660 context; cas, rac, sir, le, nuf, foh do not (left open for R9660). Hole rate 0.28 -> 0.21 (b34_sessa_holes.py).

Re-checked the first cipher paragraph of f. 141r on a full-resolution crop and built it into sentences (R9660_reading.md, R9660_en.md): 0.273 plain, 0.727 explicit holes on 11 sentences. The rest of the letter has a hole about every fifth word; R9660 kept decoded, not read.

Consistency pass (cl): 'read in part' not justified because R9660 ff. 141v-146v still need the sign-by-sign re-transcription (not-attempted kept); NOTES Status changed from read in part to in progress.

Brice Dudout (Claude Opus 5.5): R9660 ff. 141v-146v re-read sign by sign on DECODE R9660 at full size against b34 (a). Part 1's single sign written ꝍ is two signs (6 with a bar = r; z-hook over o = s), the flat-topped g is d, reversed c is q, the angle sign is ñ, part 2's 'ges' is qes (es) and its Ɉ resolved per occurrence; 124 lines changed, transcription and 25 doubtful signs frozen by SHA-256 before decoding. One pre-registered measure on those lines (one fixed key from b34's own values, 400 controls): -2.423 vs -2.453 per character for b34 (a), every control below (re-run with a quote-tracking bug fixed: -2.507 vs -2.518, controls below). 95% rule, ff. 141v-146v: sure only 69.7% -> 73.4% of tokens (the contributor's sure + probable, with context-only values, 72.0% -> 78.7%); still under the bar (dudout/README.md). The quote-bug fix was made after the first result.

Integration check of PR #480: both measure runs re-run unchanged (-2.4227 vs -2.4533; fixed run -2.5066 vs -2.5181; controls below), frozen hash prefixes match; count95 on the shipped reading file gives 2,656 sure + 190 probable of 3,587 (the committed count files say 2,634 + 188). Strict share (sure only, context-only values are holes) 69.7% -> 73.4%; the quote-bug fix was made after the first result. Images not re-fetched (login).

texts.label: R9660, Sessa, 20 Feb 1523 (RAH Salazar A-27 ff. 141r-147r)
texts.summary: The Duke of Sessa, imperial ambassador in Rome, to Charles V, from his duchy: no contemporary decipherment and not calendared by Bergenroth. Transcribed in full and deciphered in part (about 57%) with the 1524 Sessa key; the file gives each cipher line (a) with its reading (b), open groups in [ ]; it opens on letters sent 'por via de Francia' and 'la letra al duque de Bari'.

reading_review.note: 12 Nov 2026, Brice Dudout (Claude Opus 5.5): ff. 141v-146v re-read sign by sign; phrases now build on many lines (pensar, Pascua, el restante, empresa, suspende, les dio tiempo, cardenal Petru[cci], asiento que, suspicion, pedir, engañados, sin au[d]oridad, conquistar, sin duda, restitucion, el auditor, es estrecho, escusa, escriva pidiendo, podra, sucediere, despedir), but about a fifth of the tokens are still open groups or letters without sense: 73.4% of tokens sure by the README rule (78.7% with the probable words that use context-only values, the contributor's count) (dudout/r9660_141v-146v_reading_reread.txt)

texts.note: Re-read 23 Oct 2026 (b34, R9660_reread_log.md): no decipherment, copy or print reachable (seven DECODE records in RAH 9/27, none with a decipherment; f. 141r is marked 'Dup.da', the first copy not imaged; not in CSP Spain 2). The sessa1524 key values of passes 16, 17 and b23 applied (reading_r9660_b34.txt): hole rate of the decode 0.28 -> 0.21 (472 open groups or queried letters in 2,225 words). Only the first cipher paragraph of f. 141r builds sentences (R9660_reading.md, partial reading: 0.273 plain, 0.727 explicit holes). Blockers: about 100 unattested code groups (no-key-material); the court's decipherment leaves in the RAH volume (needs-physical-access); garbled spelled runs on ff. 141v-146v (not-attempted, a sign-by-sign re-transcription).

texts.label: R9665, Rome, 26 Apr 1523 (ff. 437-438)
texts.summary: A mostly clear letter on the arrest of Cardinal Soderini of Volterra, with three short cipher runs, all read: 'Su Santidad por esta bula es declarado contra Francia' (confirmed by a contemporary margin note), the Cardinal of Ancona 'muy buen servidor de V. Mt.', and 'Su Sd. mejoro ayer'. The other records of this group (R9661-R9664) are duplicates of letters Bergenroth calendared from the court's decipherments (CSP Spain 2 nos. 534, 540, 541, 544); their ciphers are not transcribed here, and R9666 is clear.

reading_review.note: The three short cipher runs read as complete Spanish phrases, two confirmed token for token by the contemporary gloss and margin note; the rest of the letter is clear. The low automatic score comes from the file layout (cipher/gloss/notes lines).

outcome.fraction_read_source: 22 Oct 2026, reading audit: only documents that build sentences count. R9665's three cipher runs (about 45 tokens) read; R9660 (1,977 cipher tokens counted on the 'a' lines of reading_r9660.txt) is decoded, not read. About 45 of 2,020 tokens, estimated. The earlier 0.55 (R9660 ~57% of tokens resolved) is withdrawn as a reading figure.
